summary: Independent verification of flow 003 on HEAD c5fde09, node v26.5.0, go1.26.1, macOS 26.5.1 arm64. Whole matrix re-run and green: typecheck exit 0; pnpm -r test exit 0 with 61 files / 320 tests / 0 failed; pnpm --filter @echolet/cli test:e2e exit 0 with 1 file / 3 tests; go test -count=1 ./... , -race and -race -tags relayv2 all exit 0 with 171 tests, 0 failures and 0 data races (the first uninstrumented pass returned cached results, so every figure quoted is from -count=1). Repository integrity checked by SHA-256 over all 973 tracked files: 971 byte-identical, the only two differing are the flow tracker's own flow.json and journal.md. No test was weakened, skipped, narrowed or deleted anywhere in the wave; the one authorised re-authoring is strictly stronger than what it replaced, verified by my own mutations rather than by the report. Nineteen mutations were run outside the tree; seventeen were killed. Two survived and are the headline findings: deleting the viewport guard on the trust modal's painted-at record leaves all 108 TUI tests green because no test ever opens a modal through the shell, and lowering LIMITS.MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES on the TypeScript side leaves 83 tests green while reintroducing RI-09's exact failure mode. Four acceptance criteria are not met (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4) and AC10 is partial: the size-closure commit 5235a6d bundles a re-authored test and a brand-new config test with the product change, so red-first ordering is unprovable for both. The wave should not close as it stands.

Re-verified still open with no wave-level record: apps/relay/relay (18094306 bytes, untracked, ignored at .gitignore:94) and three gofmt -l apps/relay files.

acceptance.criterion: AC2: no document states something the tree contradicts
acceptance.evidence: The three clauses AC2 names are clean (no clean-shutdown claim, `keryx ctx rg -i oracle docs/` returns 0 matches, no AC4-blocked paragraph, no mislabelled e2e figure). But T7 reconciled at 4346e2b and six behaviour-changing commits landed after it. Unqualified and now false: docs/STATUS_CURRENT.md limitation 3 (poll byte budget unrelated to ECHOLET_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES, contradicted by 5235a6d), limitation 4 (one undecodable record aborts the backfill; no conflict retry, contradicted by 18afa36), limitation 10 and docs/requirements/echolet-cli-prototype/README.md:37 (ticker started with no stop channel and not part of the shutdown sequence, contradicted by 18afa36), and three documents stating depr's certificate-renewal timer is not installed after T14 installed it.

acceptance.evidence: Second half met: CleanupService gained stop/stopped channels under a mutex, Stop() is wired into cmd/relay/main.go:stopBackgroundWorkAndCloseStorage on all four store-closing paths, and both pinning tests were red at 7af8492 and are green now; mutation G5 (drop r.Stop()) turns TestRelayStopsTheCleanupServiceBeforeClosingStorage red. acceptance.criterion: AC10: no test weakened, skipped, narrowed or deleted, and every fix lands after a test that failed for the right reason first, with the ordering provable from git history

artifacts.summary: Full independent verification report: matrix figures, per-AC verdicts, the two named leads, the nineteen-mutation table and thirteen findings.

findings.problem: The viewport condition on the trust modal's painted-at record - the security half of T6's D-4 - is covered by no test. Deleting `&& !isBelowMinViewport(painted)` from paint() leaves the entire TUI suite green, because no test in the repository ever opens a trust modal through runTuiShell: nothing supplies onTrustIdentifiers, and no state handed to the shell carries a modal. The renderedAt stamp and the whole answer-trust-prompt effect path are exercised at no viewport.
findings.impact: The property AC9 requires - a trust confirmation cannot be answered for identifiers that were never on screen - holds today but is unguarded. A future edit that reinstated the unconditional stamp would make a trust confirmation answerable on a 40x10 terminal for a modal whose four identifiers were never painted, and the suite would stay green. This is the same shape as the previous wave's two green-because-of-the-defect tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a shell-level test that drives runTuiShell with an injected 40x10 stdout, delivers a modal through io.onTrustIdentifiers, presses `y`, and asserts io.answerTrustPrompt was never called - together with the same scenario at 72x16 asserting it WAS called, so the pin cannot be satisfied by breaking confirmation everywhere.
findings.evidence: Out-of-tree `git archive HEAD` copy; control `npx vitest run src/tui` in apps/cli = 15 files / 108 tests passed. After deleting `&& !isBelowMinViewport(painted)`: 15 files / 108 tests passed, unchanged. `keryx ctx rg 'answerTrustPrompt|onTrustIdentifiers' apps/cli/src` returns 8 matches in 4 files, of which the only test-file matches are two inert `answerTrustPrompt: () => undefined` stubs; onTrustIdentifiers appears in no test.

findings.suggested_fix: Either give runCleanup() the work its name implies (RI-63, now unblocked because Stop() joins before the store closes), or remove the variable from the six operator-facing files and from config.Config, leaving ECHOLET_MAILBOX_TTL_HOURS as the single retention control.

The tests are good ones - I killed three mutations with them - but nobody can show from history that they ever failed for the right reason, which is exactly what AC10 asks for.

For future two-sided closures, land the new package (internal/protocol) in the test commit so the tests can be committed red.

findings.problem: The claim that one shared protocol constant governs message size on both sides of the wire is enforced in only one direction. Changing the Go mirror is caught (three tests go red). Changing the TypeScript source of truth is not: lowering LIMITS.MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES to 131072 leaves 21 files / 83 tests green in apps/cli, while the relay still accepts 262144-byte ciphertexts and may still produce poll responses up to 1 MiB. Nothing anywhere ties protocol.MaxMessageBytes (Go) to LIMITS.MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES (TypeScript), and the Go test's clientPollResponseBoundFor is a hand-written restatement of the client's rule rather than a reading of it.
findings.impact: RI-09's exact failure mode - the relay accepts and stores an envelope, answers the poll with a body above the bound the recipient enforces, the recipient refuses the whole batch, nothing is ever acknowledged and the mailbox is undeliverable while both sides look healthy - is reachable again by a one-line edit to the very constant the closure is built on, with no test red. limits.go's comment says the two must be changed together; nothing makes that true.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the Go mirror derived rather than restated: generate internal/protocol/limits.go from packages/protocol/src/constants/limits.ts, or add a check (a Go test that parses the TypeScript constant, or a JS test that parses the Go one) asserting the two numbers are equal. Pin the client's response-bound factor and wrapper on the TypeScript side too, so clientPollResponseBoundFor restates something that is itself fixed.
findings.evidence: Out-of-tree `git archive HEAD` copy. Control: `npx vitest run src/transport` = 8 files / 28 tests passed. With MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES: 524288 -> 8 files / 28 tests passed. With MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES: 131072 -> `npx vitest run src/transport src/runtime` = 21 files / 83 tests passed, Go untouched. Contrast G3: changing protocol.MaxMessageBytes from 262144 to 524288 turns TestPollResponseBoundsAreDerivedFromTheProtocolMaximum, TestMailboxPollHonoursAggregateResponseByteBudget and TestLoadDefaultsToTheProtocolMaximum red.

findings.problem: The join in Stop() - which T9 §1 calls 'the property being bought', as distinct from a Stop that merely signals - is pinned by no test. Replacing `<-stopped` with `_ = stopped` leaves internal/service and internal/server green under -race. The existing tests establish that the ticker goroutine ends and that the stop is logged before the storage close; neither establishes that Stop does not return while runCleanup is still running.
findings.impact: Harmless today because runCleanup has an empty body. The moment RI-63 gives it real Badger work - which T9 explicitly says is now unblocked - a regression to a signal-only Stop would reintroduce a transaction against a closing store, silently, with the suite green. That is the precise hazard the residual was raised about.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a service-level test whose runCleanup body blocks on a channel the test controls, asserting that Stop() has not returned while the body is in flight and does return once it completes; or, if runCleanup stays empty, record explicitly that the join is unpinned so whoever implements RI-63 pins it first.
findings.evidence: Out-of-tree copy: replacing `close(stop); <-stopped` with `close(stop); _ = stopped`, then `go test -count=1 -race ./internal/service/ ./internal/server/` -> both `ok` (service 2.313s, server 16.400s). Contrast G5 (dropping r.Stop() from cmd/relay/main.go's shutdown), which turns TestRelayStopsTheCleanupServiceBeforeClosingStorage red.

findings.problem: The unaudited-prototype notice is not present in full below roughly 20x6. tooSmallFrame wraps UNAUDITED_NOTICE to the terminal's width and renderFrame then slices the result to `rows`, so at 10x3 only the first 30 code points survive, and at 2x2 or 1x1 almost nothing does. No test covers a viewport smaller than 40x10, where the notice happens to fit in two of the ten rows.
findings.impact: AC9 asks for the notice on every frame and AC8's stated purpose is that it cannot be pushed out of view. At very small terminals it is, in the row dimension rather than the column dimension. The frames remain total and correctly shaped, so this is a completeness gap on a warning, not a crash.
findings.suggested_fix: At viewports too small to carry the wrapped notice, paint a short fallback that fits (an abbreviated 'UNAUDITED PROTOTYPE' or a truncation marker), and extend tui-shell.smallViewport.test.ts with a 10x3 case asserting whichever rule is chosen.

Whitespace-stripped containment of UNAUDITED_NOTICE: false at 1x1, 2x2 and 10x3; true from 20x6 upward. Every frame was exactly rows x cols with no ESC byte at all twelve sizes.

findings.problem: The Go restatement of the client's response-bound rule hard-codes factor 4 and a 64 KiB wrapper, while the TypeScript tests constrain the real factor only to roughly the open interval (3, 5) - relayClient.pollCapacity.test.ts accepts 3 maximum-size envelopes and refuses 5, and responseBoundDerivation accepts 1 and refuses 8 at a mocked maximum.
findings.impact: A change to pollResponseEnvelopeBudgetFactor within that interval, or to pollResponseWrapperBytes, would leave the Go restatement measuring the relay against a rule the client no longer follows, with nothing red. This is the same one-way-mirror shape as V-006 and would be closed by the same fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the client's factor and wrapper on the TypeScript side with a direct assertion on responseByteBoundFor, or derive the Go restatement from the TypeScript constants rather than restating them.
findings.evidence: Read the two constants at apps/cli/src/transport/relayClient.ts:87-88 and clientPollResponseBoundFor in the Go test; computed the interval the existing TypeScript assertions leave open (bound must exceed ~3 x 262144 to accept 3 and stay below ~5 x 262144 to refuse 5).

findings.problem: The identifier bound on /v1/prekeys/publish is pinned for bundle_id and device_id but not for identity_id: neutralising the bound leaves the identity_id subtest green, because an over-long identity_id then fails signature verification instead and still produces a typed 4xx.
findings.impact: None today - the case is refused either way. But identity_id's refusal remains incidental to its double life as the ed25519 verification key, exactly as T9 §3 described, so if identity_id ever stops being the verification key the bound would be unpinned. T9-R-5 records the related code change; this records that the subtest does not hold the bound.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert the error code for the identity_id subtest (INVALID_SCHEMA rather than any typed 4xx), so the bound rather than the signature path is what keeps it green.
findings.evidence: Out-of-tree mutation G6: change `len(identifier.Value) > MaxIdentifierBytes` to `> 1<<30` in ValidatePreKeyBundle only (the second of three occurrences). `go test -count=1 ./internal/api/handler/` -> TestPublishPreKeyBundleRejectsOversizedIdentifiersWithClientError FAILS on bundle_id and device_id; identity_id does not appear in the failure list.

findings.problem: Two FIX NOW residuals from the T1 inventory are still open on the final tree with no wave-level record of the reason: apps/relay/relay is an 18,094,306-byte untracked binary matching no commit (now matched by .gitignore:94), and three files still fail gofmt.
findings.impact: Low. The binary is ignored rather than committed, so it cannot be pushed; the gofmt files are the pre-existing RI-35 set and none of the wave's changes was added to it. Recorded because AC1 asks for a reason, and no document gives one for these two.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete apps/relay/relay (or move the build output under a build directory), run gofmt -w on the three files, or record both explicitly as deferred with the reason.

findings.problem: The push-gate diagnosis is sound and its central claim - that the gate reported a selection failure as a test failure with runner n/a and command n/a, and passed vacuously on a clean tree - is well evidenced. But the fix lives in untracked .git/hooks, T23's own §8 says keryx init/update will revert it, and both T23 and T24 remain todo, so the Go suite is still outside the gate and the change that triggered the episode was mostly Go.
findings.impact: The gate is stronger than it was for as long as the hook survives, and a fresh clone or a keryx update returns to the vacuous behaviour. No Go change can select a test, so the relay work in this wave would not have been gated even by the fixed hook.
findings.suggested_fix: Complete T23 (a repo-tracked hooks directory plus core.hooksPath, or a keryx setting that survives regeneration) and T24 (add `go -C apps/relay test -race -count=1 -tags relayv2 ./...` to the pre-push block).
findings.evidence: Read t23-push-gate-diagnosis.md in full against flow.json, where T23 and T24 are both todo. .git/hooks is untracked and outside my write scope, so I verified the diagnosis by reading it against the recorded keryx artifacts rather than by pushing.
